## REQ-MQTT-001

**MQTT v3.1.1 as minimum protocol version (client)**

A component connects to the Message Bus with MQTT v3.1.1 or a later MQTT version supported by the broker. All mechanisms of the guideline (Birth, Close and Will message, topic namespace, payloads) work with MQTT v3.1.1; a component does not depend on features of later versions (e.g. MQTT v5.0 user properties, response topic, correlation data, message expiry) for them and does not put information that other participants need into such features.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.1, SF-060
- Verification: manual, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.1-460b8388, MG-6.1-5152cb4d, MG-6.1-6ba93300, MG-6.1-76c661f1

> Open Industry 4.0 Alliance-compliant communication must use MQTT v3.1.1 as minimum protocol version.
> — MG 6.1

> All mechanisms defined in this guideline (e.g. Birth, Close and Will message, versioning of the topic namespace) work with MQTT v3.1.1 and do not require any MQTT v5.0 features.
> — MG 6.1

> MQTT v3.1.1 remains the required minimum version as long as it is sufficient for the requirements of this guideline.
> — MG 6.1

> A client may connect with a later MQTT version supported by the broker, but it must not depend on features of later versions (e.g. MQTT v5.0 user properties, response topic, correlation data, message expiry) for the mechanisms of this guideline and must not put information that other participants need into such features.
> — MG 6.1

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-001 (mandatory at all levels). Use of later versions: SF-060 (a), C-026. D7 sees the protocol version of the application under test only with a test broker it controls.

## REQ-MQTT-002

**Broker supports MQTT v3.1.1**

The MQTT broker of an OEC platform (the Message Bus) accepts MQTT v3.1.1 connections. It may additionally support later MQTT versions.

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: broker, platform
- Refs: MG 6.1, SF-060
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6.1-460b8388, MG-6.1-6ba93300, MG-6.1-f1242c63

> The broker must support MQTT v3.1.1.
> — MG 6.1

Notes: SF-060 (a), C-026. The platform requirements of the RIG are area PLT.

## REQ-MQTT-003

**Broker address provided via the Message Bus storage**

The platform makes the IP address or host name of the MQTT broker available to every container through the Message Bus storage (broker.json, RIG 4.1.1).

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: MG 6.2.1, RIG 4.1.1
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6.2.1-7407c437

> The IP address or host name of the MQTT broker is system-dependent and must be made available to any container by using the Message Bus storage (OEC Runtime & Infrastructure Guideline, 4.1.1 Message Bus Storage).
> — MG 6.2.1

Notes: The content of broker.json and the use of the Message Bus storage by a containerized application are area CNT (RIG 4.1.1, C-030). A component without container (device with its own MQTT client) gets the broker address by its own configuration.

## REQ-MQTT-004

**Broker port 8883 by default**

A component connects to the broker on port 8883 unless the Message Bus storage (SecurePort of broker.json, RIG 4.1.1) or, for a component without container, its configuration sets another port.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.1, RIG 4.1.1, SF-057
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.2.1-b440c05c

> As default setting, the port 8883 for secure communication must be used.
> — MG 6.2.1

> Through the Message Bus storage, the default might be set to a system-dependent value (OEC Runtime & Infrastructure Guideline, 4.1.1 Message Bus Storage).
> — MG 6.2.1

> The protocol version, the broker address and ports, the security settings as well as the birth message and the will message are mandatory for all levels.
> — MG 6

Notes: Keyword added in C-026 (SF-057 (a)); graded by REQ-CMP-001.

## REQ-MQTT-005

**MQTT over TLS 1.2 or higher only**

Every MQTT connection of a component to the broker is encrypted with TLS version 1.2 or higher. A component never uses a non-secure MQTT connection (e.g. port 1883).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.1, MG 6.2.2, SF-057
- Verification: d7-test, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.2.1-be806906, MG-6.2.2-5c7608e4

> The MQTT connection to the broker is always encrypted (TLS version 1.2 or higher is mandatory).
> — MG 6.2.2

> Non-secure connections (e.g. through port 1883) must not be used by clients and must not be supported by the broker.
> — MG 6.2.1

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-002. Keyword of the port 1883 sentence added in C-026 (SF-057 (a)). In a D7 test environment the broker accepts TLS only (REQ-MQTT-006), so an application that connects uses TLS.

## REQ-MQTT-006

**Broker accepts TLS connections only**

The MQTT broker of an OEC platform accepts only connections encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher; it offers no non-secure listener (e.g. port 1883).

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: broker, platform
- Refs: MG 6.2.1, MG 6.2.2, SF-057
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6.2.1-be806906, MG-6.2.2-5c7608e4

> The MQTT connection to the broker is always encrypted (TLS version 1.2 or higher is mandatory).
> — MG 6.2.2

> Non-secure connections (e.g. through port 1883) must not be used by clients and must not be supported by the broker.
> — MG 6.2.1

## REQ-MQTT-007

**Broker certificate signed by a CA**

The broker uses a certificate signed by a well-known (public) or a platform- or user-specific certificate authority (CA); self-signed broker certificates are not allowed. The certificate of the signing CA is provided as ca.pem in the OI4 certificate storage (REQ-CNT-005) or, for a different local CA, as broker_ca.pem in the Message Bus storage (REQ-CNT-001).

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: broker, platform
- Refs: MG 6.2.2, RIG 4.1.1, RIG 4.1.2, SF-057, SF-091
- Verification: d8, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6.2.2-986fbb0d

> The broker must use a certificate which is signed by a well-known (public) or a platform- or user-specific certificate authority (CA); self-signed broker certificates are not allowed.
> — MG 6.2.2

Notes: "preferably shall" replaced by "should" in C-026 (SF-057 (d)). SF-091 (g), decided by the PO in the C-030 review (2026-10-22), revises this to MUST: the client must verify the broker certificate against a CA certificate (REQ-MQTT-008). MG 6.2.2 says "must" since guideline fbe6173 (SF-091 implemented on PO order 2026-10-22). An own CA of the platform is only required if it issues certificates. Back to draft in the C-030 closure (SHOULD → MUST).

## REQ-MQTT-008

**Client verifies the broker certificate**

A component verifies the certificate of the broker when it sets up the TLS connection: the certificate chain against the CA of the Message Bus storage (broker_ca.pem; if no local CA is present, the CA of the OI4 certificate storage, RIG 4.1.2) or, for a component without container, its configured CA, and the broker address. A connection to a broker whose certificate cannot be verified is not used; an insecure mode is never the default.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.2, RIG 4.1.1, RIG 4.1.2, SF-060
- Verification: manual, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.2.2-1c096322, MG-6.2.2-e044b5e3

> The client must verify the broker certificate when it establishes the TLS connection: the certificate chain against the CA certificate (broker_ca.pem of the Message Bus storage or, if no local CA is present, the CA of the OI4 certificate storage; for a client without container, its configured CA) and the broker address.
> — MG 6.2.2

> The client must not use a connection to a broker whose certificate cannot be verified; a mode without this verification must not be the default.
> — MG 6.2.2

Notes: Added to the guideline in C-026 (SF-060 (b)). Graded by REQ-CMP-002 (security settings). D7 can check it only with a test broker that presents an untrusted certificate.

## REQ-MQTT-009

**Client authenticates to the broker**

A component authenticates itself to the Message Bus either by username and password or by a client certificate (mutual TLS).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.2, RIG 4.1.2, RIG 4.1.3
- Verification: d7-test, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.2.2-418ccec1

> The client must authenticate itself to the Message Bus either by username and password or with a client certificate (mTLS).
> — MG 6.2.2

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-002. The secrets and the client certificate are provided via the secret storage and the OI4 certificate storage (RIG 4.1.2, 4.1.3, area CNT).

## REQ-MQTT-010

**Client certificate takes precedence over username and password**

If both a client certificate with its private key and a username and password are available, a component authenticates with the client certificate.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Condition: Both a client certificate with private key and username/password are available.
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.2, SF-057
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.2.2-c84650d9

> In case a private key for an existing client certificate and username/password is available, the client certificate based authentication must be used.
> — MG 6.2.2

Notes: Keyword added in C-026 (SF-057 (c)); graded by REQ-CMP-002.

## REQ-MQTT-011

**MQTT usernames use unreserved characters only**

A username assigned for the authentication at the Message Bus contains only the unreserved characters of RFC 3986 (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, "-", ".", "_", "~") and "@". Components use the username as provided.

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: MG 1.2, MG 6.2.2, RIG 4.1.3, SF-060
- Verification: d8, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6.2.2-fc14e862

> The platform must assign usernames that only contain unreserved characters according to the RFC3986.
> — MG 6.2.2

> In addition it is also allowed to use the @ symbol.
> — MG 6.2.2

Notes: Addressed to the platform that assigns the credentials (SF-060 (d), C-026).

## REQ-MQTT-012

**The Message Bus is the communication channel of the OEC layer**

Applications and devices of the OEC layer exchange their information (data, events, configuration, lifecycle) with other participants via the MQTT broker (Message Bus); they open no other channel for this exchange. Field protocols between a connector and its assets are not affected.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.1, MG 6.2.1, SF-057
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-31ee6521, MG-6.2.1-da4b7997

> All data transmissions between the participants of the Open Edge Computing layer (applications, devices with their own MQTT client and platform services) must use the MQTT broker; no other channel is used for this exchange.
> — MG 6.2.1

> Field protocols between a connector and its assets are not affected.
> — MG 6.2.1

> Edge indicated communication - no open ports, beside MQTT (6.2.1 Broker Address and Ports)
> — MG 6.1

Notes: Keyword and scope added in C-026 (SF-057 (b)). Additional user interfaces or web services of an application (RIG 5.2) are not part of this exchange.

## REQ-MQTT-013

**MQTT ClientId – container name or unique and stable id**

A containerized application uses its container name (RIG 4.2) as MQTT ClientId. A component without container (e.g. a device with its own MQTT client) uses a ClientId that is unique on the broker and stable across reconnects, e.g. derived from its Identification Link within the length and character limits of the broker.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.3, RIG 4.2, SF-060
- Verification: manual, d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-4c5014ad, MG-6.2.3-845bb406, MG-6.2.3-e61860a9, RIG-4.2-5dfec198

> To avoid problems with length and character restrictions in some MQTT implementations, a name of the container should be used which is unique, present and accessible in any OI4 Alliance-compliant container (OEC Runtime & Infrastructure Guideline, 4.2 Container Name Conventions).
> — MG 6.2.3

> A client without container (e.g. a device with its own MQTT client) should use a ClientId that is unique on the broker and stable across reconnects, e.g. derived from its Identification Link within the length and character limits of the broker.
> — MG 6.2.3

> As MQTT ClientId, as recommended in OEC Messaging Guideline, 6.2.3 Client Identifier
> — RIG 4.2

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-009. Component without container: SF-060 (c), C-026. MQTT v3.1.1 itself requires unique ClientIds per broker.

## REQ-MQTT-014

**Keep alive interval configurable, default 60 seconds**

The MQTT keep alive interval of a component is configurable and set to 60 seconds by default.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.4
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-4c5014ad, MG-6.2.4-122db787

> The keep alive interval, counted in seconds, is configurable and should be set up to a default value of 60 seconds.
> — MG 6.2.4

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-009. The broker publishes the Will message (REQ-LIFE-008) when the keep alive of a client expires (MQTT v3.1.1).

## REQ-MQTT-015

**Clean Session true by default**

A component connects with the Clean Session flag set to true by default (no persistent session).

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.5
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-4c5014ad, MG-6.2.5-f17dc4e0

> — MG 6.2.5

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-009.

## REQ-MQTT-016

**Persistent session requires a ClientId**

A component that uses a persistent session (Clean Session false) sets a client identifier.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Condition: The component connects with Clean Session false.
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.2.5
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-4c5014ad, MG-6.2.5-07ffa981

> To use this feature, a client identifier (6.2.3 Client Identifier) must be set.
> — MG 6.2.5

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-009; MQTT v3.1.1 itself rejects an empty ClientId with Clean Session false.

## REQ-MQTT-017

**QoS 0 as default**

A component publishes and subscribes with QoS 0 by default. The QoS is chosen per hop (publisher to broker, broker to subscriber); other QoS levels may be used.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher, subscriber
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.1, SF-057
- Verification: d7-monitor
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-4c5014ad, MG-6.3.1-be1bf49a, MG-6.3.1-f257276c

> When it comes to Open Edge Computing, where there is always a strong connection on local networks, QoS 0 is sufficient: clients should use QoS 0 as the default level.
> — MG 6.3.1

> Therefore, different QoS levels can be used.
> — MG 6.3.1

Notes: Keyword added in C-026 (SF-057 (e)). Graded by REQ-CMP-009. A subscriber with QoS 2 sees the QoS of the publisher.

## REQ-MQTT-018

**No retained messages**

A component does not set the Retain flag on any message it publishes, including its Will message.

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Levels: L1 SHOULD NOT · L2 SHOULD NOT · L3 MUST NOT
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.3.2
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-4c5014ad, MG-6.3.2-e02730a2

> In context of the OI4 Alliance, the Retained message functionality is switched off by default and shall not be used.
> — MG 6.3.2

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-009. Missed messages are requested with Get. D7 detects retained messages by subscribing after the application under test has published.

## REQ-MQTT-019

**Changes are published immediately**

A publisher publishes every change of the content of a resource (e.g. an updated Data tag or a changed Health status) immediately and without external trigger on the corresponding topic, unless a publication rule configured through the PublicationList (MG 8.3.8, e.g. mode or interval) applies.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 6, MG 6.4
- Verification: d7-monitor, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-6-4c5014ad, MG-6.4-06b856de, MG-6.4-15d4253f, MG-6.4-31603ce3

> Even though this is clear to any MQTT user, it should be mentioned again; any change on a payload must be published without any external trigger on its corresponding topic.
> — MG 6.4

> E. g. when a Data tag gets updated or a Health status changes, the related topic must be published immediately.
> — MG 6.4

> Therefore, different publication rules are applicable, which can be configured through PublicationList (7.5.1 Resources).
> — MG 6.4

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-009. Health must be published on every change at all levels (REQ-TOP-017). The publication rules of the PublicationList are area RES-PUBLIST (C-027).
